data.narrative:
Summit Lithium Technologies, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Amanda Hall, has raised approximately C$120M to date. The valuation universe comprises nine Climate & Energy peers: one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the private peer set lacks sufficient depth at Summit's stage and valuation tier to support a reliable peer-median approach.

Stage-progression analysis provides the primary valuation signal. Using total capital raised of $120M as a base proxy and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A progression to subsequent stages yields $240M. This method reflects standard venture capital step-up patterns where early-stage valuations expand materially upon successful execution and advancement.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $204M to $276M, with a median point of $240M. The range reflects ±15% variance around the single applicable method. Key uncertainties include the limited comparable dataset within the narrow Climate & Energy frontier-tech peer cohort at this stage, which constrains confidence in cross-validation. Valuation sensitivity will depend on whether Summit achieves demonstrable technical or commercial milestones that strengthen positioning relative to the identified peer universe.
